picks.headline: Arc Raiders' New Machine-Learning Enemy Looks Absolutely Terrifying
picks.excerpt: The Bully is gonna get you
picks.rationale: A shipping game using machine-learned enemy behavior in a live update is concrete production use of ML, not talk. It is the most novel item in the pool and has not been covered in games before.

picks.headline: Sony PlayStation Patent Would Solve Problems With AI Vibe-Coded Patches
picks.excerpt: Anyone who's had a console knows that on a long enough timeline they will have some kind of technical bug that you need to troubleshoot, and Sony is trying to get around that reality with an AI tech support agent.
picks.rationale: New Sony patent for an AI tech-support agent that generates fixes on the console. This is a different patent from the 08-21 Kotaku grinding-AI patent card, and it signals where platform holders are aiming agentic AI.

picks.headline: Disgaea creator Sohei Niikawa has "absolutely no interest in having AI write stories instead of him"
picks.excerpt: Disgaea director Sohei Niikawa talks about generative AI use and discusses the philosophy behind his creative process.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool: a named Japanese creator draws a clear line between AI assistance and AI authorship. It is a different speaker and position from the 09-26 Kotaku card, where the NIS America head said the company is researching AI.

picks.headline: 'AI could never make Tenebris Somnia,' the 2D retro survival horror with live-action cutscenes and practical effects
picks.excerpt: A game so emotionally scarring, "you'll call your ex."
picks.rationale: Weakest pick, included only as the 4th unique fresh story. An indie studio markets live-action and practical-effects craft as its answer to AI, which fits the section's recurring human-made-positioning thread.

picks.headline: Starform's Lou Fasulo on staying at 26 people, AI-native development and who really funds a live game
picks.excerpt: The Metalstorm studio head says AI gave his 26-person team more throughput, not new capability, and explains where AI-native development stops.
picks.rationale: Most AI-substantive item left in the recovery pool: a studio head describes where AI-native production helps a 26-person live-game team and where it stops. It is a new outlet for today's set and not a duplicate. The earlier PocketGamer.biz Nordic AI-native piece from 08-26 covers different studios.
